name: Raft
rootCause: Donate Inflation ExchangeRate & Rounding Error. Lost: ~$3.2 M

descriptions.text: Donate Inflation ExchangeRate & Rounding Error. Lost: ~$3.2 M
Raft was raided by on-chain pirates for $3.3M on Friday, but the loot ended up falling overboard. When braving DeFi's stormy seas, we all must choose our vessel. Would you trust a Raft?

- Through donation and self-liquidation, the variable collateralIndex could be manipulated, thus the calculation for minted share amount could be manipulated via precision loss. - The minting in rcbETH-c uses rounding-up, which could mint 1 share instead of 0 when dust of amount collateral is added. - With shares of cbETH, attacker could redeem the shares for profits. Attack Path: (from blocksec) Attack tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0xfeedbf51b4e2338e38171f6e19501327294ab1907ab44cfd2d7e7336c975ace7 Analysis: https://x.com/BlockSecTeam/status/1723229393529835972
The stablecoin protocol Raft protocol on Ethereum was attacked and lost about $3.3 million in ETH.

Raft Finance, an Ethereum-based CDP stablecoin protocol, was exploited on November 10, 2023, due to a rounding flaw in its collateral index arithmetic. The attacker used a flash loan to inflate collateral shares, minting 6.7 billion unbacked R stablecoins. $3.3M in ETH collateral was drained, with most burned by the attacker, leaving both protocol and exploiter with net losses. A rounding error existed in Raft’s collateral share index arithmetic. By manipulating the index mid-transaction with flash-loan-scale collateral, an attacker could inflate their share count relative to actual collateral, enabling the minting of unbacked R stablecoins.
